faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: If you still cannot find the answer to your question, {emailLink} or contact our team.
faq.q1: Can I install the app on my iPhone?
faq.a1: The httpSMS application works only on Android phones at the moment since Apple doesn't allow you to install a custom SMS messaging app.
faq.q2: What's the minimum supported Android version?
faq.a2: The httpSMS Android app works from Android 9 (Pie) and above. So you can install the application on your old Android phone which you don't use anymore.
faq.q3: Can I send unlimited number of messages per month?
faq.a3: We do have packages that allow up to 200,000 SMS messages per month but you can send us an email if you will like to send more messages so we create a custom plan just for you.
faq.q4: Can I change the sender of the SMS message?
faq.a4: No you cannot. When you send an SMS message using the httpSMS app it uses your SIM card to send the message so the recipient will see your phone number as the sender of the SMS. You cannot use your brand name as the sender ID.

e2eEncryption.title: Secure your conversations with end-to-end encryption for SMS messages
e2eEncryption.description: Take control of your privacy by encrypting your SMS messages end-to-end. Safeguard your messages from prying eyes, ensuring absolute confidentiality.
e2eEncryption.seoTitle: Secure your conversations with end-to-end encryption for SMS messages - httpSMS
e2eEncryption.seoDescription: Enable end-to-end encryption for your SMS messages with httpSMS so no one but you can read the texts you send and receive through your Android phone.
e2eEncryption.intro1: We have added support for end-to-end encryption for SMS messages so that no one can see the content of the messages you send using httpSMS except you.
e2eEncryption.intro2: You setup an encryption key which you use to encrypt your messages before making an API request to httpSMS and you also use the same key to decrypt the messages you receive from httpSMS via our
e2eEncryption.algorithmNote: We are using the AES-256 encryption algorithm to encrypt and decrypt the messages.
e2eEncryption.step1Desc: the httpSMS Android app on your phone and set your encryption key under the App Settings page of the app.
e2eEncryption.step2Desc1: We use the AES-256 encryption algorithm to encrypt the SMS messages. This algorithm requires an encryption key which is 256 bits; to work around this, we will hash any encryption key you set on the mobile app using the SHA-256 algorithm so that it will always produce a key which is 256 bits.
e2eEncryption.step2Desc2: The AES algorithm also has an initialization vector (IV) parameter which is used to ensure that the same value encrypted multiple times will not produce the same encrypted value. The IV is 16 bits and it is appended to the encrypted message before encoding it in Base64.
e2eEncryption.step2Desc3: When you use our client libraries it will automatically take care of encrypting your message so you don't have to deal with creating the initialization vector and encoding the payload yourself.
e2eEncryption.step3Desc: After generating the encrypted message payload, you can send it directly using the httpSMS API. Make sure to set encrypted: true in the JSON request payload so that httpSMS knows that the message is encrypted and it will be decoded in the Android app before sending to your recipient.
e2eEncryption.step3SentNote: When you make the API request, the message will be decrypted before sending to the recipient. This is a screenshot of the SMS message which is sent to the recipient:

e2eEncryption.conclusionDesc: Congratulations, you have successfully configured your Android phone to send and receive SMS messages with end-to-end encryption.

quickstart.intro: Send your first SMS through the httpSMS HTTP API in 3 simple steps:
quickstart.step1Desc: Create your httpSMS account and copy your API key from the settings page.
quickstart.step2Desc: Download the companion Android app on your phone and sign in with your API key.

webhooksIntro.title: Introduction to Webhooks
webhooksIntro.subtitle: Receive real-time notifications on your server when messages are received, sent, delivered, or when phone heartbeat status changes.

whatIs.title: What are Webhooks?
whatIs.desc: Webhooks are automated HTTP POST requests sent by httpSMS to your server whenever a relevant event happens on your Android phone (such as receiving an incoming SMS).
whatIs.alert: Webhooks eliminate the need for continuous API polling, allowing your application to respond immediately to new SMS events.

config.title: 1. Configuring your Webhook URL
config.desc: You can configure your server endpoint URL in the settings page of the web dashboard:
config.stepDesc: Set the full URL of your endpoint (e.g. https://your-domain.com/api/webhook) and enable event forwarding.

security.title: 2. Security Signature Verification
security.desc: To ensure incoming webhook requests genuinely originate from httpSMS and were not tampered with, each request includes an x-signature header containing an HMAC SHA-256 hash of the request body.
security.secretNote: Use the Webhook Signing Secret generated in your settings page to verify the signature on every incoming request.

eventsLink.title: Explore Webhook Event Types
eventsLink.desc: View all 6 CloudEvents 1.0 JSON payload structures and field definitions.

webhookEvents.title: Webhook Events
webhookEvents.subtitle: Complete reference of all events dispatched by httpSMS conforming to CloudEvents 1.0 specifications.
webhookEvents.cloudEventsInfo: All webhook payloads dispatched by httpSMS strictly follow the open CloudEvents 1.0 JSON specification.

types.received: Dispatched when a new SMS message is received on your Android phone's SIM card.
types.sent: Dispatched when an outgoing message has been successfully transmitted over the cellular network.
types.failed: Dispatched when an outgoing message fails to send on the phone (e.g., no cell service or carrier error).
types.delivered: Dispatched when the cellular carrier delivery receipt is received.
types.heartbeatReceived: Dispatched when the Android phone sends a periodic ping confirming it is online.
types.heartbeatMissed: Dispatched when the phone fails to send a heartbeat and is deemed offline by the server.

featureControlRate.title: Control SMS Send Rate
featureControlRate.subtitle: Set limits on messages sent per minute to prevent carrier spam filtering and Android OS restrictions.

why.title: Why Control Send Rate?
why.desc1: The Android operating system includes built-in security protections that monitor outgoing SMS frequency. If too many messages are fired within seconds, the system may block the app or prompt intrusive permission dialogs.
why.desc2: Additionally, telecommunication carriers enforce automated anti-spam algorithms that temporarily throttle or block SIM cards that blast high volumes of SMS in rapid bursts.
why.carrierAlert: We recommend setting your rate limit between 10 and 20 messages per minute for reliable, uninterrupted SMS delivery.

config.title: Rate Limit Configuration
config.desc: Configure your preferred messages-per-minute rate in your account settings:
config.defaultLimitDesc: Safe and recommended default setting suitable for most day-to-day use cases.
config.maxLimitDesc: Maximum system-supported rate to prevent Android OS security interventions.

featureScheduling.title: Scheduling SMS Messages
featureScheduling.subtitle: Schedule SMS messages for future delivery via the HTTP API or Excel spreadsheets.

howItWorks.title: How does scheduling work?
howItWorks.desc: You can specify exact future timestamps when SMS messages should be pushed to your Android phone for transmission, enabling campaigns, appointment reminders, and automated alerts in advance.
howItWorks.alertMaxDays: Messages can be scheduled up to 20 days in advance.

api.desc: Simply include the send_at field in RFC 3339 format (with timezone) in your POST request body:

bulk.title: Bulk Scheduling with Excel
bulk.desc: When uploading Excel spreadsheets on the Bulk Messages page, you can define individual send times per row:
bulk.columnDesc: Fill the SendTime column with the desired date and time (e.g. 2026-08-21 14:00). If left blank, the message will send immediately respecting your configured rate limit.

featureQueue.title: Outgoing Message Queue
featureQueue.subtitle: Learn how httpSMS buffers, schedules, and dispatches messages to your Android device.

intro.title: Intelligent Queue Management
intro.desc: All outgoing messages sent to the httpSMS API enter a secure Redis/database queue before being transmitted via FCM push to your Android phone.
intro.alert: The queue guarantees zero message loss even if your device is temporarily disconnected or powered off.

rules.title: The 3 Queue Dispatch Rules
rules.desc: The dispatcher evaluates each message in the queue against three priority criteria:
rules.rule1Desc: If the message specifies an explicit future timestamp (send_at), it waits until that exact moment.
rules.rule2Desc: Bulk messages are spaced evenly according to your configured rate (e.g., every 6 seconds for 10/min).
rules.rule3Desc: If an active schedule window is configured (e.g. 08:00 to 20:00), out-of-hours messages wait until the next morning.

terms.title: Terms and Conditions of Service
terms.subtitle: Please read our guidelines, rights, and responsibilities before using the httpSMS platform.

section1.title: 1. Subject and Acceptance of Terms
section1.p1: By creating an account, downloading the companion Android app, or utilizing the httpSMS APIs (service operated by Mesa Que Vende, under Brazilian law), you agree to be bound by these Terms and Conditions.
section1.p2: If you do not agree with any of these terms, please do not use our services or applications.

section2.title: 2. SMS Gateway Operation and User Responsibilities
section2.p1: httpSMS operates as a technical integration bridge between your software applications (via HTTP API) and your physical Android phone.
section2.p2: All SMS messages are dispatched and received directly through the SIM card in your physical Android phone connected to your cellular carrier network.
section2.p3: The user is solely responsible for: (a) keeping the Android device charged, connected to the internet (Wi-Fi or mobile data), and with active cellular service; (b) paying all carrier fees and charges associated with SMS sending and mobile data; (c) ensuring full compliance with national telecommunication regulations and anti-spam laws.

section3.title: 3. Acceptable Use Policy and SPAM Prohibition
section3.p1: It is strictly prohibited to use httpSMS for: (a) unsolicited bulk messaging (SPAM); (b) phishing, financial fraud, social engineering, or spreading malicious links; (c) sending defamatory, unlawful, threatening, or infringing content; (d) any activity that violates applicable laws.
section3.p2: We reserve the right to immediately terminate or suspend accounts that violate this policy without notice or refund.

section4.title: 4. Plans, Billing, and Cancellation
section4.p1: Paid subscriptions are billed in Brazilian Reais (BRL) on a recurring basis (monthly or yearly) through our secure payment processor Stripe.
section4.p2: You can cancel your subscription at any time from your Billing dashboard. Cancellation prevents future charges and your access remains active until the end of the paid period.
section4.p3: In accordance with Brazilian Consumer Protection Law, a 7-day right of withdrawal applies to initial plan purchases.

section5.title: 5. Limitation of Liability
section5.p1: httpSMS is not liable for: (a) delayed, failed, or undelivered messages caused by mobile carrier network outages or destination handset issues; (b) SIM card blocks enacted by telecom operators for spam detection; (c) phone disconnections, battery failure, or lost network signal.
section5.p2: The service is provided 'as is', with commercially reasonable efforts made to maintain 24/7 cloud infrastructure availability.

section6.title: 6. Governing Law and Jurisdiction
section6.p1: These Terms are governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Federative Republic of Brazil, notably the Brazilian Internet Civil Framework (Law No. 12,965/2014) and General Data Protection Law (LGPD - Law No. 13,709/2018).
section6.p2: The courts of the Judicial District of São Paulo/SP, Brazil, shall have exclusive jurisdiction over any disputes.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy (LGPD Compliance)
privacy.subtitle: Learn how we collect, store, and protect your personal data in accordance with the Brazilian General Data Protection Law (LGPD).

section1.title: 1. General Information and Data Controller
section1.p1: This Privacy Policy governs the processing of personal data by httpSMS (operated within the Mesa Que Vende ecosystem, São Paulo, Brazil).
section1.p2: We are committed to protecting your privacy and treating your data transparently and securely in strict compliance with the LGPD (Law No. 13,709/2018) and Marco Civil da Internet (Law No. 12,965/2014).

section2.title: 2. Data We Collect
section2.p1: We collect the following categories of data to provide our SMS gateway services:
section2.item1: Account Data: Full name, email address, and authentication credentials (Firebase Auth).
section2.item2: Message Metadata: Sender phone number, recipient phone number, timestamps, and delivery status.
section2.item3: Message Content: Temporarily processed to forward and display messages. When end-to-end encryption (AES-256) is enabled, content is stored strictly ciphertext, inaccessible to httpSMS staff.
section2.item4: Billing Information: Payment transactions are processed directly by Stripe in a PCI-DSS certified environment. We do not store credit card numbers on our servers.
section2.item5: Connection and Access Logs: IP address, access timestamps, and app diagnostic logs retained in compliance with Brazilian law.

section3.title: 3. Legal Bases and Processing Purposes
section3.p1: Data processing is performed under the following legal bases of LGPD:
section3.item1: Contract Performance (Art. 7, V): To deliver SMS gateway functionality, account management, and support.
section3.item2: Legal Obligation (Art. 7, II): Connection log retention under Marco Civil da Internet and tax compliance.
section3.item3: Legitimate Interest (Art. 7, IX): Fraud prevention, platform security, and service reliability.

section4.title: 4. End-to-End Encryption
section4.p1: We provide native support for AES-256 end-to-end encryption. When configured, message bodies are encrypted on your backend before transmission and decrypted solely on your Android device. Neither httpSMS nor intermediaries can read encrypted message contents.

section5.title: 5. Third-Party Service Providers
section5.p1: We do not sell or rent personal information. Data is shared strictly with essential infrastructure providers:
section5.item1: Google Cloud Platform / Firebase: Cloud hosting and authentication.
section5.item2: Stripe: Secure payment and subscription processing.
section5.item3: Neon PostgreSQL & Upstash Redis: Encrypted database and message queue infrastructure.

section6.title: 6. Data Subject Rights (LGPD)
section6.p1: Under Article 18 of LGPD, you have the right to:
section6.item1: Confirm the existence of and access your personal data;
section6.item2: Correct incomplete, inaccurate, or outdated data;
section6.item3: Request anonymization, blocking, or deletion of unnecessary or excessive data;
section6.item4: Request data portability or full deletion of your account and personal records;

section7.title: 7. Data Protection Officer (DPO) Contact
section7.p1: To exercise your privacy rights or submit questions regarding data handling, contact our Data Protection Officer via our support email.
